lesson_title: Your Black Pen Is Hiding Colours
hook_text: Put a dot from a black felt-tip on wet paper and watch it explode into blue, purple and yellow.
clip_script: Draw a pencil line on a paper strip, put a black dot on it, and stand it in a little water. The water climbs, grabs the ink and carries it up. Each colour travels at its own speed, so the black splits apart. Black ink was a mixture all along. That is chromatography, and labs use it to catch drug cheats and check food colourings. Two more tricks for things a filter cannot separate. Want salt from seawater? Evaporate. On the West Coast, the Sun dries seawater in shallow pans and leaves salt crystals behind; the water is lost to the air. Want pure water from seawater? Distil. Boil it, catch the steam on something cold, and pure drops form while the salt stays behind. Keep the solid, or keep the liquid: pick your method.
visual_style: Whiteboard paper strip with a black dot blooming into coloured bands; a salt pan under a blazing Sun; a pot lid dripping clear drops back into a beaker.
pacing: Fast colour reveal first, then two quick contrasting methods.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and try the black-pen experiment at home.
